title: Europe's Missing AI Advantage
excerpt: Why data infrastructure — not model size — may determine Europe's position in the next phase of AI competition.
body:
Why data infrastructure — not model size — may determine Europe's position in the next phase of AI competition.

## The argument in brief

Most coverage of AI sovereignty fixates on model scale: who has the biggest cluster, the most parameters, the fastest chips. This misses where Europe's actual leverage lies.

**European data spaces** — the shared, interoperable data infrastructure being built across health, energy, mobility, and other sectors — could become the raw material advantage that model size alone can't buy. Access to well-governed, high-quality European data is not something a larger US or Chinese model can simply route around.

### Why this matters now

The window is narrow. As [the EU's own Technological Sovereignty Package](https://ec.europa.eu) makes clear, the regulatory scaffolding for data spaces is already being built — but the actual data-sharing agreements that would make them useful are still thin on the ground.

If European institutions treat data spaces as a compliance checkbox rather than a genuine competitive asset, the advantage disappears before it's realised. *That's the real risk* — not that Europe fails to build a frontier model, but that it fails to make the one asset it does have actually usable.
